items.title: Vali Makes It Two In A Row, Finn Strikes Back | Leogang DH World Cup
items.description:
This week we're joined by Alan Milway, Neko Mullaly and Olly Morris to break down all the action from an incredible weekend of World Cup downhill racing.

From Vali's dominant home victory to Finn Iles' winning run, revised race schedules, tyre choices and track evolution, we cover it all.

New episode out now: https://youtu.be/VwR_KmQ7XwE

Thanks to BOA for supporting this week's show. Learn more about BOA here:

www.boafit.com

items.title: Leogang World Cup Breakdown | What Actually Went On
items.description:
Vali Höll continued her incredible start to the season with a second consecutive World Cup victory at Leogang, while Finn Iles secured a huge win in the men's race. But was this the weekend that changed the trajectory of the 2026 Downhill World Cup season?

In this week's Downtime Podcast post-race show, we're joined by Neko Mullaly, Olly Morris and Alan Milway to break down all the action from the Leogang UCI Downhill World Cup.

We discuss Höll's dominant home victory in front of a huge Austrian crowd, extending her winning streak and strengthening her position as the rider to beat this season. We also dive into Finn Iles' winning run, the impact of the revised race schedule, track evolution, tyre choices, changing conditions and the key moments that shaped the podiums.

As always, expect detailed race analysis, technical insight, paddock observations and plenty of post-race banter from one of the most exciting downhill weekends of the year.

items.title: The Team NOBODY Saw Coming | Neko Mullaly on Finding Asa Vermette and Building Frameworks
items.description:
In this episode of Just Ride, Rob Warner and Eliot Jackson sit down with Neko Mulally to talk about building Frameworks Racing from the ground up, from homemade bike prototypes to one of the most talked-about teams in downhill mountain biking.

Neko shares the story behind signing Asa Vermette, bringing Aaron Gwin onto the team, developing World Cup race bikes, and creating a team culture built around trust, performance, and progression. The conversation dives into bike setup, rider development, Hardline, American downhill racing, and what it really takes to compete at the highest level.

They also discuss the future of Frameworks, growing the sport in the U.S., and why simplicity, confidence, and passion still matter in modern downhill MTB.
